articles.title: Veil: a local-first redaction gate for everything you paste into an AI
articles.excerpt: Last week I pasted a production database URL into a chat window. Nothing happened. That is exactly the problem. The paste box sits one keystroke away from the stack trace, the config file, the support…
articles.body: Last week I pasted a production database URL into a chat window. Nothing happened. That is exactly the problem. The paste box sits one keystroke away from the stack trace, the config file, the support ticket with a customer's name in it. Every AI chat UI warns you not to paste secrets, and then puts the box right there. I built Veil to sit between the clipboard and the chat box. It runs on your machine, finds the credentials and the quieter contextual leaks, and replaces them with stable placeholders before anything is sent.

articles.excerpt: Perplexity SPACE is an open-sourced isolated execution engine that runs AI agents in a safe sandbox. Perplexity launched it in October 2026 as the infrastructure behind its Computer assistant. The pit…
articles.body: What Is Perplexity SPACE Perplexity SPACE is an open-sourced isolated execution engine that runs AI agents in a safe sandbox. Perplexity launched it in October 2026 as the infrastructure behind its Computer assistant. The pitch is simple: AI agents need to run code and browse the web. But you do not want them touching your real filesystem or your real network. SPACE gives agents a sandbox that is isolated, reproducible, and safe. I tested SPACE for a week with a few different AI agents. Here is my honest review.

articles.title: # Your packages haven't migrated to `material_ui`. Can you?
articles.excerpt: Where we left off In the previous article, I migrated a small app from the SDK's Material to the material_ui package and measured every step. The app had no third-party UI package, on purpose. The res…
articles.body: Where we left off In the previous article , I migrated a small app from the SDK's Material to the material_ui package and measured every step. The app had no third-party UI package, on purpose. The result: seventeen automatic fixes, one fix by hand, and the same ten tests green before and after. Plus three things dart fix misses. Real apps are not like that. They use a font package, a router, a form widget, something to render Markdown. And for each of these packages, the same question comes back: has it migrated yet? I said I would add real packages to that app. I built a second one instead, so that each package has a natural place in it, and nothing from the first app can hide a result. It uses four packages. Two of them have already published a migrated version. Two have not.

articles.title: Building an AI Agent with Human Approval Gates
articles.excerpt: To add human approval gates to an AI agent, put a policy layer between the model's tool calls and the code that runs them. Give every tool a risk tier, and let tiers rise based on arguments. Low-risk…
articles.body: To add human approval gates to an AI agent, put a policy layer between the model's tool calls and the code that runs them. Give every tool a risk tier, and let tiers rise based on arguments. Low-risk calls run straight away. High-risk calls go into an approval queue and wait for a named person. Blocked actions never run. Any request that nobody answers before its deadline counts as denied . Log every decision as structured events. The model doesn't make any of these choices. Your code does. Below is a complete, tested implementation in about 200 lines of standard-library Python, with a scripted demo, an approver CLI, tests, and an adapter for a real LLM. Where should the approval gate sit? Put it outside the model, at the single point where tool calls become side effects.

articles.title: MCP Security Checklist: Hardening Model Context Protocol Servers Before Production
articles.excerpt: To harden a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for production, do eight things. Authenticate every HTTP request with OAuth tokens issued for your server. Map each tool to one narrow scope. Validate i…
articles.body: To harden a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for production, do eight things. Authenticate every HTTP request with OAuth tokens issued for your server. Map each tool to one narrow scope. Validate inputs beyond the JSON Schema. Treat tool output as untrusted text. Rate-limit and time out every call. Write a tamper-evident audit log. Keep secrets out of the model's context. Pin your tool definitions so they can't change without review. The rest of this post turns each item into code you can run, in TypeScript and Python, checked against the current MCP specification (revision 2026-07-28). This is a follow-up for teams whose MCP server already works. If you have never built one, start with a basic tutorial first.

articles.excerpt: Three years ago I watched a seller in Hangzhou move $40,000 of skincare in a four-hour stream from a room the size of a parking space. No agency, no ad budget - just a phone, a ring light, and a scrip…
articles.body: Three years ago I watched a seller in Hangzhou move $40,000 of skincare in a four-hour stream from a room the size of a parking space. No agency, no ad budget - just a phone, a ring light, and a script she had clearly run a thousand times. That script is the product. Not the product she was selling - the script itself , the pacing, the offer structure, the way she re-opened every 90 seconds for the people who had just arrived. In China, that operational knowledge is an industry. In the US, where TikTok Shop is growing fastest, most sellers are still improvising it alone. So I spent the last weeks building Live Selling Playbook - an open knowledge base that translates China's live-selling operating system into English, for US TikTok Shop sellers.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.body: Tom Cruise has built a career out of playing larger-than-life characters, but some of his best performances are when he delves into the more vulnerable people beneath the movie-star bravado. Days of Thunder filters the story of a hotshot NASCAR driver through the humbling process of learning to trust someone, while Jerry Maguire finds a sports agent in the throes of learning that success means little without genuine human connection. Even Tropic Thunder , for all its outrageous comedy, gives Cruise room to disappear into a grotesque Hollywood executive whose insecurities are as ridiculous as his explosive temper. And Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Digger gives Cruise one of his most fascinating character studies yet as an oil tycoon with a brazen plan to save the world.

articles.body: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
